newsitem.title: UK: Bayoil fixes tanker from Ceyhan for Iraqi crude.
newsitem.headline: Bayoil fixes tanker from Ceyhan for Iraqi crude.

text.p: U.S. trader Bayoil has provisionally fixed a 337,000 deadweight tonne tanker to sail with Iraqi crude from the Turkish port of Ceyhan, ship brokers said on Friday.
Brokers said the company had fixed the Ultra Large Crude Carrier (ULCC) Concordia 1 for prompt lifting of crude oil on subjects for four days.
This means Bayoil has the option of confirming the fixture within four days.

Oil traders around the world are waiting nervously for signs of the restart of Iraq crude oil exports, which will flow from Ceyhan, the site of an export terminal for piped Iraqi crude, as well as the Iraqi Red Sea port of Mina al-Bakr.
Under the current phase of the oil-for-food deal with the U.N. which came into effect on June 8, Baghdad is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over 180 days.
A delay over U.N. approval of Iraq's plan for aid distribuion has held off the flow of oil for this period.

If exports start in early to mid August, these delays mean Baghdad will have to sell oil at a rate of two million barrels per day (bpd) in order to reach a $1 billion cash target by an early September interim deadline.
But analysts reckon Iraq's export capacity may be no more than 1.3 million bpd.
U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said on Thursday he expected the aid distribution plan to be approved early next week.

Industry officials said some eight million barrels, or around 1.1 million tonnes of Iraqi crude are currently held in storage at Ceyhan, left over from a previous oil-for-food deal which is an exemption from a wider package of sanctions on Iraq.
Brokers also said on Thursday Bayoil had been enquiring about chartering large tankers from Mina al-Bakr too but did not confirm any specific fixture.
